title: Hybridization Involving s and p Orbitals
topicTitle: Hybridization involving s and p orbitals only
notes:
## 1. Topic Introduction — Mixing Orbitals to Point Bonds

Carbon's ground-state configuration (1s² 2s² 2p²) promises two bonds; methane delivers four identical ones at 109.5°. The rescue is **hybridisation**: before bonding, the central atom's s and p orbitals of the same shell blend into new **equivalent hybrid orbitals**, whose shapes and directions are tailor-made for bonding. sp³ → tetrahedral, sp² → trigonal planar, sp → linear — three recipes that rationalise the shapes VSEPR counts (and the NEB 2024 methane question directly).

## 2. Fundamental Concepts

### 2.1 What hybridisation is (and is not)

- **Definition:** the intermixing of orbitals of slightly different energies (same shell: one s + p orbitals) to form an equal number of **identical hybrid orbitals**, oriented for maximum overlap.
- Key features: number of hybrids = number of atomic orbitals mixed; hybrids have **one large lobe** (better overlap → stronger bonds); hybridisation happens **at the moment of bonding**, not in the free atom; it needs **promoted electrons** (energy invested, repaid by stronger bonds).
- It is a **mathematical convenience turned physical picture** — the orbitals that point where the bonds point.

### 2.2 The three s–p recipes

| Type | Mix | Hybrids | Geometry | Angle | Leftover p |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| sp³ | 1 s + 3 p | 4 | tetrahedral | 109.5° | none |
| sp² | 1 s + 2 p | 3 | trigonal planar | 120° | 1 p ⟂ |
| sp | 1 s + 1 p | 2 | linear | 180° | 2 p ⟂ |

### 2.3 Worked molecules

- **CH₄ (sp³):** C is excited to 2s¹2p³; four sp³ hybrids point to a tetrahedron's corners; four σ (sp³–s) bonds; H–C–H = 109.5°. Also NH₃, H₂O — same sp³ set, but lone pairs occupy hybrids and compress angles (107°, 104.5°).
- **C₂H₄ / BF₃ (sp²):** three sp² hybrids in a plane at 120°; the unused p orbital stands perpendicular — in ethene it forms the π bond (topic 33); in BF₃ it stays empty (Lewis acid).
- **C₂H₂ / BeCl₂ (sp):** two sp hybrids at 180°; two leftover p orbitals — in ethyne, two π bonds build the triple bond; in BeCl₂, two σ (sp–p) bonds give linear BeCl₂.
- **Extension (NEB 2024 asked): SF₆ and IF₇** — SF₆ is sp³d² (octahedral, 90°); IF₇ is sp³d³ (pentagonal bipyramidal) — d-orbital hybridisations beyond the s–p syllabus, but quotable as VSEPR-consistent extensions.

### 2.4 Hybridisation and bond strength

- Hybrid orbitals overlap more effectively (large directed lobe) than pure p orbitals — bonds are stronger and shorter.
- More s-character → stronger, shorter bond and larger angle: sp (50% s) > sp² (33%) > sp³ (25%). Ethyne's C–H (sp) is the strongest C–H bond in organic chemistry.

## 3. Scientific Definitions

| Term | Scientific meaning | Value to quote |
|---|---|---|
| **Hybridisation** | Intermixing of same-shell orbitals to form equivalent directed hybrids | sp³, sp², sp |
| **sp³ hybrid** | 1 s + 3 p → 4 equivalent orbitals, tetrahedral | CH₄: 109.5° |
| **sp² hybrid** | 1 s + 2 p → 3 hybrids, trigonal planar + 1 p ⟂ | C₂H₄: 120° |
| **sp hybrid** | 1 s + 1 p → 2 hybrids, linear + 2 p ⟂ | C₂H₂: 180° |
| **s-character** | Fraction of s in the hybrid; ↑ → stronger, shorter bonds | sp 50% > sp² 33% > sp³ 25% |

## 4. Detailed Explanation

### 4.1 Verified PYQ (NEB 2024/04): what is hybridisation? Show sp³ explains methane

- **Definition** (section 2.1), then the methane argument:
- Ground-state C: 1s² 2s² 2p² — only two unpaired electrons → predicts CH₂.
- **Promotion:** 2s electron promoted to 2p → 2s¹ 2p³ (four unpaired; energy cost paid back fourfold by stronger bonds).
- **Hybridisation:** 2s + three 2p blend → four equivalent sp³ hybrids, each with one electron, directed to a tetrahedron's corners (109.5°).
- **Bonding:** each hybrid overlaps head-on with H's 1s → four identical σ bonds, all H–C–H = **109.5°** — matching experiment exactly (VSEPR's domain count and VBT's orbital picture agree).

### 4.2 Ethene and ethyne — hybrids plus leftover p orbitals

- **C₂H₄:** each C sp²; three sp² per carbon (two C–H σ + one C–C σ), the perpendicular p orbitals overlap sideways → π. Planar, 120°.
- **C₂H₂:** each C sp; two sp per carbon (one C–H σ + one C–C σ), two leftover p orbitals per carbon → **two π bonds** (perpendicular pair of π clouds). Linear, 180°; C≡C 120 pm.

### 4.3 NH₃ and H₂O — sp³ with occupants

- Both N and O use four sp³ hybrids; in NH₃ one hybrid holds a lone pair (3 BP + 1 LP → pyramidal, 107°); in H₂O two hold lone pairs (2 BP + 2 LP → bent, 104.5°).
- Hybridisation explains the *electron geometry*; lone-pair repulsion (VSEPR) explains the *observed shape* — the two theories are complementary, not rival.

**sp, sp², sp³ — geometry, examples, s-character effects**

| Hybrid | Mixed from | Geometry / angle | π orbitals left | Examples |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| sp | 1 s + 1 p | Linear 180° | 2 | C₂H₂, BeCl₂, CO₂ |
| sp² | 1 s + 2 p | Trigonal planar 120° | 1 | C₂H₄, BF₃, graphite |
| sp³ | 1 s + 3 p | Tetrahedral 109.5° | 0 | CH₄; NH₃ 107°; H₂O 104.5° |

## 5. Comparison Tables

**The three hybridisations at a glance**

| Property | sp | sp² | sp³ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Orbitals mixed | 1s + 1p | 1s + 2p | 1s + 3p |
| Hybrids formed | 2 | 3 | 4 |
| Geometry | Linear | Trigonal planar | Tetrahedral |
| Angle | 180° | 120° | 109.5° |
| s-character | 50% | 33% | 25% |
| Leftover p | 2 | 1 | 0 |
| σ capacity | 2 | 3 | 4 |
| Examples | C₂H₂, BeCl₂, CO₂ | C₂H₄, BF₃, SO₂ | CH₄, NH₃, H₂O |

**Hybridisation vs VSEPR — division of labour**

| Question | Answered by |
|---|---|
| How many domains? | VSEPR (Lewis structure count) |
| What electron geometry? | VSEPR (domain arrangement) |
| Which orbitals make the bonds? | Hybridisation (sp/sp²/sp³) |
| Why is the angle compressed? | VSEPR (lone-pair repulsion) |

## 6. Common Confusions

**Hybridisation is per-bonding-event, not a free-atom property:** an isolated carbon does not "contain" sp³ orbitals; they exist in the molecule, formed as bonds form.
**Lone pairs occupy hybrids too:** NH₃ and H₂O are sp³ — the lone pairs sit in sp³ hybrids; that is why their angles are near-tetrahedral rather than 90°.
**More p-character ≠ stronger bond:** s-character strengthens (closer to nucleus) — sp bonds beat sp³ bonds in strength and shortness.

## 7. Exam Application

**Verified PYQ (NEB 2024/04): What is hybridisation? Show how sp³ hybridisation explains the shape of methane.** — Hybridisation is the intermixing of atomic orbitals of comparable energy on the same atom to form an equal number of equivalent, identically oriented hybrid orbitals. **Verified PYQ (NEB 2024/04): Predict the shape and hybridisation of SF₆ and IF₇.** — **SF₆:** six bond pairs → octahedral, sp³d² (d²sp³), all angles 90°. **IF₇:** seven bond pairs → pentagonal bipyramidal, sp³d³ — five equatorial I–F at 72°, two axial at 90°. Both exceed the s–p syllabus (d orbitals involved) but follow the same logic: hybrids = domains.

**NEB-style (3m): Explain the formation of the ethyne molecule using hybridisation.** — Each carbon is sp hybridised: promotion, then 2s + 2pₓ → two sp hybrids at 180°, leaving two perpendicular p orbitals. One sp on each C overlaps head-on → C–C σ; the other sp overlaps H's 1s → C–H σ (linear H–C≡C–H). The two pairs of parallel p orbitals overlap sideways → **two π bonds** (mutually perpendicular clouds). Result: linear molecule, C≡C = 120 pm, strongest C–H bonds (50% s-character).
confusion: **sp³ ≠ four bonds always:** NH₃ (3 bonds) and H₂O (2 bonds) are sp³ — the hybrid count is four; bonds are what remain after lone pairs occupy hybrids.
**Promotion is an investment, not a loss:** the promotion energy is repaid by the extra bond energies of four strong sp³ bonds versus two weak pure-p bonds.

practiceQuestions: **NEB 2024 (3m): What is hybridisation? Show how sp³ hybridisation explains the shape of methane.** — **Definition:** hybridisation is the intermixing of atomic orbitals of nearly equal energy on the same atom to form an equal number of equivalent hybrid orbitals oriented for maximum overlap. **Methane:** ground-state carbon (1s²2s²2p²) has only two unpaired p electrons — insufficient for four bonds. One 2s electron is **promoted** to 2p (2s¹2p³, four unpaired electrons; the promotion energy is repaid by forming two extra strong bonds). The 2s and three 2p orbitals then **hybridise** into four equivalent sp³ hybrids directed toward the corners of a tetrahedron. Each hybrid overlaps head-on with a hydrogen 1s orbital → four identical σ bonds with **H–C–H = 109.5°** — the observed tetrahedral shape, with all four C–H bonds equal in length and strength.

**NEB 2024 (2m): Predict the shape and hybridisation of SF₆ and IF₇.** — **SF₆:** sulphur forms six bond pairs with no lone pair → six electron domains → **octahedral shape, sp³d² hybridisation**, all F–S–F angles 90°. **IF₇:** iodine forms seven bond pairs → **pentagonal bipyramidal shape, sp³d³ hybridisation** — five equatorial I–F bonds at 72° to each other and two axial bonds at 90°. Both require d-orbital participation (period ≥ 3), extending the sp/sp²/sp³ series by the same "hybrids = domains" rule.

**NEB-style (3m): Using hybridisation, describe the bonding in ethyne (C₂H₂) and compare its C–H bonds with ethane's.** — Each carbon is **sp hybridised**: after promotion, 2s + one 2p mix into two sp hybrids at 180°, leaving two mutually perpendicular unhybridised p orbitals. One sp hybrid of each carbon overlaps head-on → the C–C σ bond; the other sp overlaps a hydrogen 1s → C–H σ. The two pairs of parallel p orbitals overlap sideways → **two π bonds** with perpendicular clouds, completing the triple bond (C≡C, 120 pm). The molecule is **linear (180°)**. **Comparison:** ethyne's sp hybrids carry 50% s-character versus ethane's sp³ 25% — s electrons sit closer to the nucleus, so ethyne's C–H bonds are **stronger and shorter** (106 pm vs 109 pm), and their carbon acidity is correspondingly higher.
formulas:
- sp³: 4 hybrids, 109.5°; sp²: 3 hybrids + 1p, 120°; sp: 2 hybrids + 2p, 180°
- s-character: sp 50% > sp² 33% > sp³ 25%
- Bond strength/shortness ∝ s-character
keyPoints: Hybridisation: same-shell s+p orbitals mix → equivalent directed hybrids; number conserved; large lobes overlap better. sp³ (4, tetrahedral 109.5°): CH₄, NH₃, H₂O. sp² (3, trigonal planar 120° + 1 p ⟂): C₂H₄, BF₃, SO₂. sp (2, linear 180° + 2 p ⟂): C₂H₂, BeCl₂, CO₂. s-character ladder sp > sp² > sp³ in bond strength. Extensions: SF₆ sp³d² octahedral; IF₇ sp³d³ pentagonal bipyramidal (NEB 2024).
summary: Hybridisation is the orbital answer to VSEPR's shape count: same-shell s and p orbitals blend into equivalent, strongly directed hybrids — four sp³ pointing to a tetrahedron (CH₄ at 109.5°), three sp² in a plane (C₂H₄, BF₃ at 120°, one p orbital left over for π), two sp in a line (C₂H₂, BeCl₂ at 180°, two p orbitals for two π bonds). The mechanism needs promotion (carbon's 2s²2p² → 2s¹2p³) — an investment repaid by stronger, shorter bonds, since hybrid lobes overlap better and extra s-character (sp 50% > sp² 33% > sp³ 25%) pulls electrons closer. Lone pairs occupy hybrids too — NH₃ and H₂O are sp³ with angles compressed to 107° and 104.5° by VSEPR repulsion. Beyond the s–p syllabus the same rule extends: SF₆ sp³d² octahedral, IF₇ sp³d³ pentagonal bipyramidal (NEB 2024). Domain count gives the hybrid type; the leftover p orbitals give the π bonds; the shape follows.
importantStatements: "Hybridisation is the process of intermixing of orbitals of slightly different energies so as to redistribute their energies, resulting in the formation of new set of orbitals of equivalent energies and shape."
importantNotes: Verified PYQs: NEB 2024/04 — hybridisation definition + sp³ methane, and SF₆/IF₇ shapes (solved above); NEB 2023's ethene question (sp²) solved in topic 33. Other items are NEB-style practice.

**Verified PYQ (NEB 2024/04): Predict the shape and hybridisation of SF₆ and IF₇.** — **SF₆:** six bond pairs → octahedral, sp³d² (d²sp³), all angles 90°. **IF₇:** seven bond pairs → pentagonal bipyramidal, sp³d³ — five equatorial I–F at 72°, two axial at 90°. Both exceed the s–p syllabus (d orbitals involved) but follow the same logic: hybrids = domains.

**NEB-style (3m): Explain the formation of the ethyne molecule using hybridisation.** — Each carbon is sp hybridised: promotion, then 2s + 2pₓ → two sp hybrids at 180°, leaving two perpendicular p orbitals. One sp on each C overlaps head-on → C–C σ; the other sp overlaps H's 1s → C–H σ (linear H–C≡C–H). The two pairs of parallel p orbitals overlap sideways → **two π bonds** (mutually perpendicular clouds). Result: linear molecule, C≡C = 120 pm, strongest C–H bonds (50% s-character).
confusion: **sp³ ≠ four bonds always:** NH₃ (3 bonds) and H₂O (2 bonds) are sp³ — the hybrid count is four; bonds are what remain after lone pairs occupy hybrids.
**Promotion is an investment, not a loss:** the promotion energy is repaid by the extra bond energies of four strong sp³ bonds versus two weak pure-p bonds.
keyPoints: Hybridisation: same-shell s+p orbitals mix → equivalent directed hybrids; number conserved; large lobes overlap better. sp³ (4, tetrahedral 109.5°): CH₄, NH₃, H₂O. sp² (3, trigonal planar 120° + 1 p ⟂): C₂H₄, BF₃, SO₂. sp (2, linear 180° + 2 p ⟂): C₂H₂, BeCl₂, CO₂. s-character ladder sp > sp² > sp³ in bond strength. Extensions: SF₆ sp³d² octahedral; IF₇ sp³d³ pentagonal bipyramidal (NEB 2024).
importantConcepts: Hybridisation and VSEPR agree by construction: the domain count from VSEPR equals the hybrid count from VBT — use VSEPR for shape, hybridisation for the orbital explanation behind it.
examples: ***Methane's four identical bonds*** — impossible for raw 2s/2p orbitals (one s bond would differ from three p bonds); sp³ mixing makes all four equivalent, as NMR and bond lengths confirm.
universalFacts: Ethyne's sp C–H bonds (50% s-character) are acidic enough (pKₐ ≈ 25) to form acetylides with strong bases — hybridisation strength you can deprotonate.
importantStatements: "Hybridisation is the process of intermixing of orbitals of slightly different energies so as to redistribute their energies, resulting in the formation of new set of orbitals of equivalent energies and shape."
importantNotes: Verified PYQs: NEB 2024/04 — hybridisation definition + sp³ methane, and SF₆/IF₇ shapes (solved above); NEB 2023's ethene question (sp²) solved in topic 33. Other items are NEB-style practice.
examShortTricks: Count domains → hybrid: 2 sp, 3 sp², 4 sp³, 5 sp³d, 6 sp³d², 7 sp³d³. s-character: "sp 50, sp² 33, sp³ 25 — more s, stronger, shorter, wider angle."

- s-character: sp 50% > sp² 33% > sp³ 25%
- Bond strength/shortness ∝ s-character

practiceQuestions: **NEB 2024 (3m): What is hybridisation? Show how sp³ hybridisation explains the shape of methane.** — **Definition:** hybridisation is the intermixing of atomic orbitals of nearly equal energy on the same atom to form an equal number of equivalent hybrid orbitals oriented for maximum overlap. **Methane:** ground-state carbon (1s²2s²2p²) has only two unpaired p electrons — insufficient for four bonds. One 2s electron is **promoted** to 2p (2s¹2p³, four unpaired electrons; the promotion energy is repaid by forming two extra strong bonds). The 2s and three 2p orbitals then **hybridise** into four equivalent sp³ hybrids directed toward the corners of a tetrahedron. Each hybrid overlaps head-on with a hydrogen 1s orbital → four identical σ bonds with **H–C–H = 109.5°** — the observed tetrahedral shape, with all four C–H bonds equal in length and strength.

**NEB 2024 (2m): Predict the shape and hybridisation of SF₆ and IF₇.** — **SF₆:** sulphur forms six bond pairs with no lone pair → six electron domains → **octahedral shape, sp³d² hybridisation**, all F–S–F angles 90°. **IF₇:** iodine forms seven bond pairs → **pentagonal bipyramidal shape, sp³d³ hybridisation** — five equatorial I–F bonds at 72° to each other and two axial bonds at 90°. Both require d-orbital participation (period ≥ 3), extending the sp/sp²/sp³ series by the same "hybrids = domains" rule.

**NEB-style (3m): Using hybridisation, describe the bonding in ethyne (C₂H₂) and compare its C–H bonds with ethane's.** — Each carbon is **sp hybridised**: after promotion, 2s + one 2p mix into two sp hybrids at 180°, leaving two mutually perpendicular unhybridised p orbitals. One sp hybrid of each carbon overlaps head-on → the C–C σ bond; the other sp overlaps a hydrogen 1s → C–H σ. The two pairs of parallel p orbitals overlap sideways → **two π bonds** with perpendicular clouds, completing the triple bond (C≡C, 120 pm). The molecule is **linear (180°)**. **Comparison:** ethyne's sp hybrids carry 50% s-character versus ethane's sp³ 25% — s electrons sit closer to the nucleus, so ethyne's C–H bonds are **stronger and shorter** (106 pm vs 109 pm), and their carbon acidity is correspondingly higher.

universalFacts: Ethyne's sp C–H bonds (50% s-character) are acidic enough (pKₐ ≈ 25) to form acetylides with strong bases — hybridisation strength you can deprotonate.

mindmap.centralConcept: sp, sp2 and sp3 hybridization in organic molecules

subtopics.name: Sigma and pi frames
points: Sigma bonds form by head-on overlap and lie along the internuclear axis
Pi bonds form by sideways overlap and lie above and below the axis
Only unhybridized p orbitals can form pi bonds

subtopics.name: Worked assignments
points: Ethane C2H6: both carbons sp3, all single bonds, free rotation
Ethene C2H4: both carbons sp2, one pi bond, planar, no rotation
Ethyne C2H2: both carbons sp, two pi bonds, linear

subtopics.name: Mixed examples
points: Benzene: every carbon sp2, giving a planar ring with delocalised pi electrons
Acetaldehyde CH3CHO: CH3 carbon sp3, carbonyl carbon sp2
Carbon dioxide: carbon sp hybridized, two pi bonds

subtopics.name: Reading hybridization from structure
points: Count sigma bonds plus lone pairs on the atom — that is the steric number
An atom with one double bond and two single bonds is sp2
Hybridization explains geometry; geometry does not explain hybridization
